title: The Asylum
synopsis: You wake on an iron bed in Cell Block C of an asylum that closed fifty years ago. The PA system hums to life. The Night Warden has been expecting you, and he doesn't like patients who wander.
artStyle: abandoned Victorian asylum, peeling paint, cold blue moonlight, flickering caged bulbs, film grain
intro: Good evening, my patients. Lights out was hours ago, and yet here you are, awake. How restless. The doors of my ward are locked, as they have always been. If you want to leave, you will have to earn it, together. I'll be listening on the PA. I am always listening. Your treatment begins now.
escapedText: The gate grinds open onto wet grass and moonlight. Behind you, the PA gives one last crackle: 'Discharged. For now.' You run, and you don't look back.
failedText: Every door in the ward slams at once. The bulbs go out one by one, and the PA hums a lullaby. 'Back to bed, my patients. We'll try again tomorrow.'

gameMaster.name: The Night Warden
gameMaster.persona: Speaks over the asylum's crackling PA system in a soft, sing-song voice, like a nurse doing rounds at three in the morning. Calls the group 'my patients'. Never raises his voice: the calmer he sounds, the worse it is. Treats every solved lock as a worrying symptom.

stages.title: Cell Block C
stages.description: Three iron beds, bolted to the floor. The paint on the walls hangs in long strips, and a bulb flickers behind a wire cage. Barred window, a drain in the floor, a bucket in the corner. The cell door has a small observation slot, locked from the outside, and a patient chart hangs from the end of your bed.

objects.label: barred window
objects.look: Moonlight through the bars. Scratched into the sill, over and over: {key:scratches}

objects.label: flickering bulb
objects.look: It buzzes behind its wire cage. On, off. On, off.

objects.label: peeling paint
objects.look: Long strips of paint. Behind one, someone has scratched tally marks into the plaster.

objects.label: mattress
objects.look: Thin and stained. Something hard is sewn into the lining.

objects.label: bedframe
objects.look: Iron, bolted to the floor. A strip of tape is stuck underneath.

objects.label: floor drain
objects.look: You fish down the drain with the magnet on its string. Click. The key comes up, dripping.
objects.lockedText: Something glints far down the drain, below the grate. Your fingers can't reach it.

objects.label: bucket
objects.look: An empty tin bucket. You'd rather not know what it was for.

objects.label: cell door
objects.look: Solid steel. There's a keyhole on the inside, which makes no sense for a cell.

objects.label: chalk marks
objects.look: Chalk tallies on the wall, and under them an old reflex hammer.

objects.label: rusty tap
objects.look: Scratched into the tap's collar: back {key:scratches}.

objects.label: iron bed leg
objects.look: Someone has carved into the bed leg: back {key:scratches}.

stages.title: The Treatment Wing
stages.description: A long corridor of white tiles. Wheelchairs stand in a row, as if waiting for someone. A nurses' desk, a gurney, a linen cart and a laundry chute line the walls. At the far end, a glass medicine cabinet glows under a single lamp, beside a staff locker and a security door with a card reader.

objects.label: notice board
objects.look: Visiting hours, crossed out. A timetable for treatments nobody remembers.

objects.label: cracked sink
objects.look: The tap drips in a slow, steady rhythm.

objects.label: filing tray
objects.look: Empty forms, all signed by the same Warden.

objects.label: laundry chute
objects.look: A cold draught blows up from far below.

objects.label: medicine cabinet
objects.look: Glass shelves of pill bottles, glowing under the lamp.

objects.label: staff locker
objects.look: Grey metal, dented. A riddle is written inside its little window.

objects.label: wheelchairs
objects.look: A row of wheelchairs, each a different colour. A drawer with a keypad is fixed under the last one.

objects.label: nurses' desk
objects.look: A cold cup of tea, a ringing phone that never rings.

objects.label: gurney
objects.look: A sheet over a gurney. Only pillows underneath, thank goodness.

objects.label: linen cart
objects.look: Folded sheets, starched stiff.

stages.title: The Records Room
stages.description: Filing cabinets tower to the ceiling, their drawers hanging open. A desk, a card index and a radiator line the room, and an X-ray light box hangs dark on the wall. An old reel-to-reel tape player is wired into the exit gate, which has a heavy keyhole and a three-digit keypad.

objects.label: filing cabinets
objects.look: Drawers of patient files. Every photograph has been removed.

objects.label: shelf of tapes
objects.look: Reels of tape, each labelled with a date and a patient number.

objects.label: padded panel
objects.look: Under the UV light, words bloom across the padding in the Warden's hand: {key:warden-word}
objects.lockedText: A padded panel, torn at the seams. Nothing you can see.

objects.label: records desk
objects.look: A typewriter with a half-finished report. It stops mid-word.

objects.label: X-ray light box
objects.look: Under the UV penlight, a table of symbols appears on the film: {key:case-file}
objects.lockedText: A dead X-ray light box with blank film clipped to it. Or is it blank?

objects.label: card index
objects.look: Index cards in faded ink. One is missing.

objects.label: exit gate
objects.look: Iron bars, a heavy keyhole and a three-digit keypad.

objects.label: radiator
objects.look: Stone cold. It hasn't been on in fifty years.

objects.label: notes tray
objects.look: A symbol card slipped between two files: {key:case-file}

objects.label: desk blotter
objects.look: Pressed under the blotter, another symbol card: {key:case-file}

objects.label: intercom
objects.look: A code sheet taped behind the intercom: {key:warden-word}

objects.label: orderly's cart
objects.look: A code sheet under the towels: {key:warden-word}

puzzles.title: The Observation Slot
puzzles.prompt: A word lock holds the slot in your cell door shut. The PA crackles: 'I can fill your whole cell, yet I take up no space at all. Tell me what I am, and I'll let you look.'
hints: Look up at that flickering bulb.
Flick a switch and the cell is full of it.
puzzles.solvedText: The slot scrapes open. A key on a loop of hospital string drops through, bounces once and vanishes down the floor drain. Only the string is left on your side.

variants.prompt: A word lock holds the slot in your cell door shut. The PA crackles: 'Speak my name and I am gone. Tell me what I am, and I'll let you look.'
hints: The PA has just gone very quiet. What's left?
It's broken the moment anybody talks.

variants.prompt: A word lock holds the slot in your cell door shut. The PA crackles: 'I follow you everywhere in the light, and I vanish when it's gone. Tell me what I am, and I'll let you look.'
hints: Look at the wall behind you under the flickering bulb.
It copies every move you make, and it's always right behind you.

puzzles.title: The Cell
puzzles.prompt: Search your cell properly: the mattress, the peeling paint and the bedframe.
hints: Three things in the cell are worth a closer look.
Search the mattress, the peeling paint and the bedframe.
puzzles.solvedText: Sewn into the mattress lining, taped under the bedframe, hidden behind the paint: the pieces of a small, strong magnet. You fit them together.

puzzles.title: The Cell Door
puzzles.prompt: The cell door is solid steel, with a keyhole on the inside. A cell should never lock from the inside.
hints: The key that came through the slot is down the drain. You'll need to fish it out.
Tie the magnet to the string, fish the key out of the drain, then use it on the door.
puzzles.solvedText: The key turns with a clunk. The door swings out into a long, tiled corridor. The PA sighs: 'Oh dear. Wandering again.'

puzzles.title: The Patient Chart
puzzles.prompt: Clipped to the chart is a little lockbox marked MEDICATION, with a 3-digit dial. Someone has scribbled the code across the chart's pages. Each of you read a different page.
hints: Every phone holds one of the digits, written as a fact. Say them out loud, in order.
In order: {facts}.
puzzles.solvedText: The lockbox opens. There's no medicine inside, only a note in shaky handwriting: 'Don't believe the Warden's clock.'

generator.pieceTemplate: Scrawled across your page of the chart in red pen: the {ordinal} digit is {fact}.

puzzles.title: The Scratched Wall
puzzles.prompt: Scratched into the wall above your bed by a previous patient, in a scramble: {cipher}. The chart's lockbox has a second lock that wants the word.
hints: There's more than one number around the room. Only one of them turns this into a real word.
The previous patient left a number somewhere near the window.
Move every letter back along the alphabet by that number.
puzzles.solvedText: The second lock gives. Inside, a photograph of the ward in happier days, with one face circled.

puzzles.title: The Medicine Cabinet
puzzles.prompt: The glass medicine cabinet has a 3-digit lock. A typed label on the glass reads: '{order}. Take as directed.'
hints: Each phone saw one colour of pill bottle, and how many of them there were.
Read them in the label's order: {order}.
puzzles.solvedText: The cabinet clicks open. Among the bottles, one rattles differently from the others. You take it.

generator.pieceTemplate: You counted the {color} pill bottles on the cabinet's shelves: there were {digit}.

puzzles.title: The Wheelchairs
puzzles.prompt: The wheelchairs in the corridor: {items}. The drawer under the last one has a keypad. A card taped to it: 'Each chair's place, 1 nearest the door, in the order I list them.'

generator.pieceTemplate: Written on a torn treatment slip in your pocket: {clue}

hints: Each phone holds a fact about the chairs. Put them all together.
Start with the chair you're surest of, and mark each spot yes or no.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The drawer slides open. Inside: a nurse's penlight with a violet bulb.

puzzles.title: The Mirror Writing
puzzles.prompt: Painted across the tiles in the Warden's folded alphabet: {cipher}. A word lock on the nurses' desk drawer waits.
hints: The Warden folds the alphabet in half.
A is Z, B is Y, C is X… Read it letter by letter.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The drawer clicks open. Only a list of patients inside, every name crossed out.

puzzles.title: The Light Board
puzzles.prompt: The nurses' station has a board of call lights, all jammed. Each switch flips its light and the ones beside it. Light them all.
hints: Work from the top row down: fix each row with the switches below it.
Press {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Every call light glows at once. Down the corridor, a buzzer sounds, and the PA laughs softly.

puzzles.title: The Staff Locker
puzzles.prompt: The orderly's locker has a word lock. Written inside the little window in marker: 'I have keys but open no locks. I have space but no room. You can enter, but you can never go inside.'
hints: Think about the computer at the nurses' station.
You type on it.
puzzles.solvedText: Inside the locker hangs a staff rota. Every name on it has been crossed out but one, written in fresh ink: yours.

variants.prompt: The orderly's locker has a word lock. Written inside the little window in marker: 'I have a head and a tail, but no body. Flip me to decide your fate.'
hints: Check your pockets.
Heads or tails?

variants.prompt: The orderly's locker has a word lock. Written inside the little window in marker: 'The more I dry, the wetter I get.'
hints: Think about the washrooms down the hall.
You use one after a bath.

puzzles.title: The Security Door
puzzles.prompt: The security door at the end of the wing has a card reader, blinking red. A sign beneath it: STAFF ONLY.
hints: You need something only the staff would carry.
Look closely at the pill bottle that rattles, then use what's inside on the reader.
puzzles.solvedText: The reader beeps green and the door hisses open. Just inside, on the floor, as if someone left it for you: a heavy iron master key.

puzzles.title: The Patient Numbers
puzzles.prompt: The file drawers are stamped with patient numbers: {sequence}. The last drawer is locked, and its keypad wants the next one.
hints: Look at how each number changes to the next.
The next number is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The drawer opens on your own file. The photograph is recent.

puzzles.title: The Tape Player
puzzles.prompt: The reel-to-reel tape player is wired to the gate's second lock. A label on it reads: 'Repeat the Warden's three words, first to last.'
hints: Three phones each remember one word the Warden whispered over the PA.
Say them in order, first to last, like: word word word.
puzzles.solvedText: The reels stop turning. '{answer},' the Warden repeats softly. 'Good. You were listening.' One lock on the gate falls open.

generator.pieceTemplate: You heard it on the PA as you ran down the corridor: the {ordinal} word the Warden whispered was '{word}'.

puzzles.title: The Case File
puzzles.prompt: A case file is stamped in symbols, a word from the doctors' notes: {cipher}. The gate's second keypad has a letter lock too.
hints: There's more than one key card around. Only one is real: it reads a word that fits the clue.
The symbols need a key. Something that only shows up in the right light.
Shine the UV penlight on the X-ray light box, then read the symbols.
puzzles.solvedText: The letter lock clunks open. Inside the case file, a single line: 'Patient is not to be released.'

puzzles.title: The Warden's Last Word
puzzles.prompt: The PA ticks by itself, a slow pattern of short and long clicks, a word for the night: {cipher}
hints: There's more than one key card around. Only one is real: it reads a word that fits the clue.
Short and long clicks need a key. The Warden wrote it somewhere only UV light can find.
Shine the penlight on the padded panel, then read the clicks letter by letter.
puzzles.solvedText: The clicking stops. The PA is silent for the first time since you woke.

puzzles.title: The Exit Gate
puzzles.prompt: The gate takes the master key AND a 3-digit code. Painted on the wall beside it: 'Your cell's number, then the floor you woke on, then how many beds you shared.'
pieces: You remember the number stencilled on your cell door: 7.
You remember the sign in the stairwell: FLOOR 1.
You remember your cell: 3 iron beds, bolted down.
hints: Three phones remember three numbers. Put them in the order painted on the wall.
The cell number, then the floor, then the beds.
puzzles.solvedText: The master key turns and the keypad glows green. With a groan of old iron, the gate begins to open.

pieces: You remember the number stencilled on your cell door: 4.
You remember the sign in the stairwell: FLOOR 2.
You remember your cell: 5 iron beds, bolted down.
You remember the number stencilled on your cell door: 9.
You remember the sign in the stairwell: FLOOR 3.
You remember your cell: 6 iron beds, bolted down.

items.name: Hospital string
items.description: A loop of hospital string. The key that was tied to it is gone.

items.name: Magnet
items.description: Small and strong, rebuilt from three pieces.

items.name: Magnet on a string
items.description: The magnet tied to the hospital string. Good for fishing.

items.name: Key on a string
items.description: Small and cold, dripping from the drain.

items.name: Rattling pill bottle
items.description: Brown glass. It rattles, but not like pills.
items.inspect: You tip it out: no pills, just a staff pass, rolled tight, with the photo scratched off.

items.name: Staff pass
items.description: A laminated staff pass with a magnetic strip. The photo has been scratched out.

items.name: UV penlight
items.description: A nurse's penlight with a violet bulb. Some writing only shows up under it.

items.name: Iron master key
items.description: Heavy and old. Stamped on the bow: WARD C.

items.name: Reflex hammer
items.description: A little rubber hammer for testing knees. It doesn't fit any lock.

recipes.text: You knot the string around the magnet. A fishing line, of sorts.
